## OVERVIEW

In Unit 3 we examine the foundations of the collaborative data-intensive improvement (CDI) model and get a gentle introduction to working with documents and text as data. The required and self-selected readings for this week focus on three major influences on the CDI model and also provide a survey of general overview of text mining in education. In addition, we'll take a look a three broad approaches to analyzing text as data including lexical-based methods, supervised and unsupervised machine learning.

## READINGS

In addition to watching the Unit 3 Intro video, this week you'll be required to read **Chapter 5** from [Learning Analytics Goes to School](https://catalog.lib.ncsu.edu/catalog/NCSU4862134), an article introducing text mining methods in education, and one self-selected journal article, conference presentation, or scholarly resource to help address our discussion questions for the week.

### Required

-   Krumm, A., Means, B., & Bienkowski, M. (2018). Chapter 5: Foundations of Collaborative Applications of Educational Data Mining and Learning Analytics. *Learning analytics goes to school: A collaborative approach to improving education*. Routledge. <https://doi.org/10.4324/9781315650722>
-   Fesler, L., Dee, T., Baker, R., & Evans, B. (2019). Text as Data Methods for Education Research. *Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness*, *12*(4), 707–727. <https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2019.1634168>

### Self-Selected Resource 

Use the [NCSU Library](https://www.lib.ncsu.edu/#articles), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/) or search engine of your choice to locate a journal article, presentation, website or other scholarly resource that addresses a topic of interest and includes one or more of the following terms or related terms:

-   text mining
-   sentiment analysis
-   topic modeling
-   text classification
-   lexical- or dictionary-based methods
-   text networks
-   term frequency - inverse document frequency

Your selection should also address one or more of the discussion topics/questions provided below. In addition, you are welcome to find less formal resources such as videos or shorter online articles to share with the class and that help us better understand this week's topics for discussion.

### 1) LA Goes to School Chapter 5: Foundations of Collaborative Applications of Learning Analytics

-   What educational context (real or hypothetical) are you interested in better understanding or improving through collaborative data-intensive approaches?
-   How might one of the foundational approaches described in Chapter 5 be applied to this context?
-   What specific characteristics, processes, or tools of this approach might you utilize, and for what purpose?

### 2) Text as Data: Methods for Education Research

-   How might text mining be used to expand research questions, improve validity and representativeness, or reduce the cost of research?
-   What text-based data source might you analyze, and what would count as a single “document” (e.g., essay, tweet, discussion post) in your dataset?
-   What research question might you address using automated text analysis methods, which method would you choose, and how would you prepare your text for analysis?

## ASSIGNMENT

### Grading

#### **Quantity (3pts)**

-   Three original posts, one in each thread above, plus one peer reply.

#### **Quality (3 pts)**

-   Offer **new or insightful contributions** that move the conversation forward. No strict word count; aim for substance.
-   Across your posts, reference the **course text** and your **self-selected resource** (and any assigned videos, if relevant).
-   Use the model below to guide how you contribute. Table 1 of [Gao's productive online discussion model](https://github.com/sbkellogg/eci-586/blob/main/unit-1/lit/Gao-productive-discussion.pdf) (summarized below)

At minimum, your collective posts should also help us interpret or elaborate on discussion topics, questions, or ideas others have shared by "making connection to the learning materials" and should reference at some point the required video, course text and your self-selected resource.

### Productive Online Discussion Model

#### **Disposition 1: Discuss to Comprehend**

Actively engage in such cognitive processes as interpretation, elaboration, **making connections to** prior knowledge.

-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to the **learning materials**
-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to **personal experience**
-   Interpreting or elaborating the ideas by making connection to other **ideas, sources, or references**

#### **Disposition 2: Discuss to Critique**

Carefully **examine other people's views**, and be sensitive and analytical to conflicting views.

-   Building or **adding new insights or ideas** to others' posts
-   **Challenging ideas** in the texts
-   Challenging ideas in others' posts

#### **Disposition 3: Discuss to Construct Knowledge**

Actively **negotiate meanings**, and be ready to reconsider, refine and sometimes revise their thinking.

-   **Comparing views** from the texts or others' posts
-   Facilitating thinking and discussions by **raising questions**
-   Refining and **revising one's own view** based on the texts or others' posts

#### **Disposition 4: Discuss to Share Improved Understanding**

Actively **synthesize knowledge** and explicitly express improved understanding based on a review of previous discussions.

-   **Summarizing personal learning** experiences of online discussions

-   **Synthesizing content** of discussion

-   **Generating new topics** based on a review of previous discussions
